title: Anatomy-Activated Mixture-of-Experts for 3D Medical Vision-Language Pre-training
claim: Standard routers gate experts on visual features alone; ours also conditions routing on an explicit composition histogram plus a structural prior.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, bottom-to-top flow, extra histogram branch in right panel
description: Two side-by-side diagrams share the same skeleton, with data flowing bottom to top. Panel (a), titled 'MoE routing', has a row of blue token squares T_i feeding a peach 'Router' box. The router fans out arrows to K pink FFN boxes (FFN1, FFN2, ..., FFNK). Each FFN output goes through a circled-cross multiplication node. All of these merge into a circled-plus summation node with an output arrow above. Panel (b), titled 'A²MoE routing', repeats this structure. Its router input is richer: blue tokens T_i and a green organ-histogram vector h̃ combine into an orange embedded vector Ψ(h̃). That vector is added to a purple affinity matrix Ã ∈ R^{C×K} at a plus node. A small bar chart with colored organ bars (colon, spleen, liver, {organ}) sits at the lower right. The eye goes first to the extra input branch in (b), which is the only difference between the panels.
caption: Comparison of MoE routing strategies. (a) MoE routing: The input feature map $x$ is pooled to form a global visual context, which is passed through an MLP router to produce logits over $K$ experts. Softmax-normalized weights are then used to compute a convex combination of expert outputs $E_k(x)$. Routing depends solely on visual features. (b) In addition to visual context, a foreground-normalized organ-composition histogram $\widetilde{\mathbf h}$ is embedded and fused with visual features to jointly condition the router. Each foreground entry represents the corresponding organ's share of the total foreground voxel mass in the input crop. A learnable class-to-expert affinity matrix $\mathbf A^{(s)}$ introduces a structural prior via a log-probability term $\log(\widetilde{\mathbf h}\widetilde{\mathbf A}^{(s)}+\epsilon)$, biasing expert selection toward anatomically consistent assignments. The resulting logits are softmax-normalized to obtain routing weights, and the final output is computed as a weighted sum of expert responses.
abstract: Medical Vision-Language Pre-training (VLP) leverages the semantic richness of radiology reports to learn 3D representations, yet current architectures remain fundamentally anatomy-agnostic. While clinical diagnostics rely on organ-specific context, standard encoders apply a uniform, dense parameterization to all volumetric patches, and existing Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routers gate on isolated local features without explicit access to the organ composition of the scan or crop. We propose Anatomy-Activated Mixture-of-Experts (A$^{2}$MoE), a framework that incorporates anatomical inductive biases within the model's computational path. A$^{2}$MoE introduces two key components: (1) a Histogram Representation Router (HRR) that conditions expert selection on global visual context and a predicted anatomical composition histogram, encouraging anatomy-dependent expert weighting; and (2) an Organ-Query Multi-Scale Projector (OQMSP) that utilizes learnable queries to extract organ-level embeddings for fine-grained alignment without requiring manual annotations at inference. By routing at the patch level rather than the token level, A$^{2}$MoE reduces routing complexity by orders of magnitude while satisfying load balancing by construction. Pre-trained on over 60,000 multi-phase CT scans, A$^{2}$MoE achieves state-of-the-art performance across segmentation, classification, and detection benchmarks. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our anatomically grounded inductive biases support robust generalization to MRI and ultrasound, establishing a scalable foundation for medical representation learning. The code is available at https://github.com/gmum/A2MoE.
